To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cost of reducing global carbon dioxide emissions is approximately US$10 per tonne of carbon in 2010 prices, and that the cost of meeting the Kyoto target is approximately $30 per tonne of CO2.

(1) the global cost of CO2 emissions reductions is less than 0.5 percent of world income in the first period of the model (2000-2005), less than 1.0 percent of world income by the second period (2005-2010) and less than 2 percent of world income after that; and (2) the costs are less than 1 percent of income in the first decade of the model for all but the most stringent emissions reduction targets.
The costs of CO2 reduction depend crucially on whether or not one takes into account the effects of CO2 emissions on the world economy and the effects of CO 2 abatement on the world economy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the costs of CO, emissions abatement in the context of global economic and environmental change.
the costs of CO 2 emission reduction from a global perspective.
identifying least cost mitigation strategies and with assessing the implications for the global economy and for individual countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) the cost of CO2 emission reduction is not large in the short-term; (2) the cost of emission reduction is not very sensitive to the choice of abatement strategy; and (3) the cost of abatement rises substantially over time.
the cost of CO2 emission abatement depends critically on the specific mitigation strategy and on the time horizon considered.
global CO2 emissions abatements costs are in the range 2-5% of global GDP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the global economy is more flexible than previously thought and can adjust to the constraints imposed by the need for a CO2 emissions reduction.
global CO2 emissions can be reduced by about 20% at a cost of about 0.2% of world GDP per annum.
the global economic system is not as fragile and brittle as many people believe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost of reducing CO2 emissions depends on how this is done.
the costs of CO emissions abatement can be substantially reduced if global abatement efforts are coordinated.
global CO2 emission reductions can be achieved at a relatively low cost.
